ATS-Friendly Resume Templates & Formats

A visually striking resume template can silently fail an ATS scan if it uses tables, columns, text boxes or icons the parser can't read. Here's what actually matters in a resume format.

Guided Resume BuilderResume Score Checker

What makes a template ATS-friendly

  • •Single-column layout — multi-column templates often get scrambled by ATS parsers
  • •Standard section headers ("Experience", "Education", "Skills") instead of creative labels
  • •No text inside tables, images, headers/footers, or embedded graphics
  • •Standard, widely available fonts (Arial, Calibri, Georgia) rather than decorative fonts
  • •Reverse-chronological order for work experience, which both ATS and recruiters expect by default

Formatting mistakes that break parsing

  • •Contact info placed inside a header/footer — many parsers skip these entirely
  • •Skills or dates inside tables — some ATS engines read tables in the wrong order or drop them
  • •Icons used instead of text labels for email/phone/LinkedIn
  • •Non-standard date formats that confuse automatic experience-duration calculations

Choosing a format for your experience level

Freshers and early-career candidates should generally stay to one page and lead with education/projects if work experience is limited. Experienced professionals (5+ years) can extend to two pages, leading with a strong work-experience section.

Frequently asked questions

Should I use a Word template or build from scratch?

Either works as long as it stays single-column with standard headers — the safest approach is starting from a guided builder that produces ATS-safe structure by default.

Is a one-page resume mandatory?

For freshers and early-career roles, yes as a strong default. Experienced professionals with 8+ years can justify a second page if every line adds real value.
